newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil- Prices soften after recent hike.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil- Prices soften after recent hike.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market was weaker on Wednesday as buying interest decreased with many players staying away from the market searching for fresh directions after Tuesday's hike, traders said.
A major sold 20,000 tonnes of 180-cst grade to a local trading company at $102 per tonne, down from Tuesday's $104.5 trading level, for lifting between March 29 and April 2.
Offers were heard at $104 per tonne.
Local buyers have been pushing up prices in the past few days, but the fall in prices today prompted many traders to wonder if Tuesday's hike was indicative of real cash fundamentals.
Most traders prefer to adopt a wait and see stance before moving their cargoes.
"People are trying to get a clear China picture before they take the next move, so not many of them want to trade at this moment," said one independent.
Despite few enquiries from China, Chinese players remained largely inactive. Chinese importers has been staying away from the market since the early February Lunar New Year holidays, traders said.
Fuel oil swaps ended off softer with March at $101.00/102.50 against Tuesday's $101.75/$102.75.
Traders said scheduled maintenance turnarounds in Singapore later this month could fuel demand and pushed prices higher.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
